sections.h2: Where do you go for property tax in Bladen County, NC?
sections.html:
Bladen County Tax Administration is at 201 E King Street in Elizabethtown, open Monday through Friday from 8:30 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. The mailing address is PO Box 385, Elizabethtown, NC 28337, the phone is 910-862-6730, and the email is bctax@bladenco.org.

Bills can be viewed and paid through the county's online portal, or by phone through the automated line at 1-877-369-0025. A separate property record search lets owners check parcel data and last year's values.

Starting with the 2026 tax year, the county also collects the bills for four towns: East Arcadia, Bladenboro, White Lake and Elizabethtown. Owners inside those towns should ask Tax Administration how the town portion appears on the bill.

sections.h2: What should a seller know about Bladen County itself?
sections.html:
Bladen is a rural Coastal Plain county in southeastern North Carolina, and the county government describes it as the fourth largest in the state at about 879 square miles. The Cape Fear River bisects it, White Lake is commercially developed for visitors, and Jones and Singletary Lakes are state parks.

Census QuickFacts puts the July 2025 population at 30,007, which is up 1.3% from the 2020 base but well under the 35,190 counted in 2010. The 2020-2024 median value of an owner-occupied home is $135,100, against $332,700 nationally. About 69.2% of housing is owner-occupied, the median gross rent is $773, and 97 building permits were issued in 2025.

The county names food processing, manufacturing and assembly, textiles, chemicals and agribusiness as its industry base, with workforce training at Bladen Community College. For an owner, the practical point is that a back-tax or title problem is large next to a $135,100 median value.

sections.h2: Did Bladen County's 2026 revaluation change my 2026 tax bill?
sections.html:
No. The General Assembly postponed Bladen's new values by a year, so 2026 bills use the older 2025 values and the 2026 reappraisal values first apply for the 2027 tax year.

The county had finished a reappraisal effective January 1, 2026, using an outside appraisal firm, and mailed value notices to every real property owner on March 9, 2026. Its last reappraisal before that was in 2022. Then S.L. 2026-8 and S.L. 2026-47 imposed a one-year moratorium. The legislative staff summary lists Bladen among nine counties subject to it: Anson, Bladen, Buncombe, Chowan, Davidson, Guilford, Onslow, Pamlico and Pender.

A School of Government analysis of the first bill notes that counties must still list and appraise changes found during the reappraisal, such as an unrecorded building, but use the older schedule of values. It also says counties should send notice of the new values again in 2027. Watch for that notice, because the 2027 value is the one that will govern your bill, and confirm its status with Tax Administration at 910-862-6730 before you list a house.

sections.h2: How do appeals work after the Bladen reappraisal?
sections.html:
The county's own appeal period for the 2026 notices ran until April 10, 2026, and that date has passed. The two session laws also say taxpayers in affected counties may appeal their 2026 values during calendar year 2026, which the School of Government reads as an extension through December 31, 2026.

The county FAQ says an affordability concern is not a ground for appeal. Valid grounds are inequitable assessment compared with similar properties, or errors on the property record card. Request the record card before you file, and gather support such as a private fee appraisal, comparable sales, a survey, or photographs of structural damage.

  • Mail the detached notice portion to the revaluation team at PO Box 774, Elizabethtown, NC 28337
  • Drop it in the box in the lobby at 201 E King Street
  • Use the drop box in the parking lot behind the Bladen County Courthouse

Under state law the board of equalization and review decides formal appeals. It first meets between the first Monday in April and the first Monday in May, and a reappraisal-year board finishes by December 1. A further appeal goes to the Property Tax Commission within 30 days after the board mails its decision.

sections.h2: How does Bladen County's tax rate compare with other 2026 reappraisal counties?
sections.html:
The Department of Revenue's 2024-25 schedule lists Bladen at $.7850 per $100, and the Association of County Commissioners' 2026 map book also shows 0.7850 for fiscal year 2026-27. Bladen is one of several counties that were scheduled to reappraise in 2026.

The county FAQ states that appraisal and tax rate are separate decisions. Values are set first, and the commissioners set the rate in June from the budget. A higher value therefore does not by itself raise a bill.

sections.h2: When is Bladen County tax due and what relief can owners apply for?
sections.html:
Bladen taxes follow the state calendar: due September 1, payable without interest through January 5, then 2% on January 6 and three-fourths of one percent a month from February 1. The statutory listing period for property runs through January 31.

The county posts two separate application deadlines on its Tax Administration page:

  • New applications for the elderly or disabled exclusion, the disabled veteran exclusion and the circuit breaker are due by June 1 each year.
  • New applications for other exemptions and deferments, such as religious, charitable and present-use valuation, are due by January 31 each year.

NCDOR prints $38,800 as the income limit for the 2026 tax year for elderly or disabled relief and circuit breaker, with $58,200 as the 150% figure. The disabled veteran exclusion removes the first $45,000 of appraised value and has no age or income limit. An owner can receive benefit from only one of the three programs, and the circuit breaker needs a new application every year.

sections.h2: What does a seller need to know about taxes and deeds in Bladen County?
sections.html:
The register of deeds will not accept a deed without proof that taxes are handled. It accepts a deed only with a completed certification form, or without the form if a closing attorney prepared it and the deed carries this statement: delinquent taxes, if any, are to be paid by the closing attorney to the county tax collector upon disbursement of closing proceeds.

That is why a house with back taxes can still close. The attorney pays the delinquent bills from the sale proceeds, and the deed then goes to the register. State law adds that the seller pays the deed excise tax of $1.00 per $500 of value before recording.

When the county forecloses on a tax lien and the property does not sell at auction, it becomes county property and stays available for sale. The county posts a list of those properties, last updated November 2, 2026. State tax foreclosure sales run on a public auction, a possible deposit of up to 20%, and a 10-day window for increased bids after the report of sale. An owner who sells before confirmation can stop the process by paying taxes, penalties, interest and costs.

faqs.q: What is the phone number for Bladen County Tax Administration?
faqs.a: The phone number is 910-862-6730. The office is at 201 E King Street in Elizabethtown and is open Monday through Friday, 8:30 a.m. to 5:00 p.m.

faqs.q: Why are Bladen County's new 2026 property values not on my 2026 bill?
faqs.a: The General Assembly delayed the reappraisal by one year for Bladen and eight other counties. The 2026 bill uses the 2025 values, and the new values first take effect for the 2027 tax year.

faqs.q: Is the deadline to appeal the Bladen County reappraisal over?
faqs.a: The county's April 10, 2026 deadline has passed, but the session laws allow appeals of 2026 values during calendar year 2026. Call Tax Administration to confirm your status, and watch for the 2027 notice, which opens the next appeal round.

faqs.q: When must a Bladen County homeowner apply for elderly, disabled or veteran tax relief?
faqs.a: New applications for those three programs are due by June 1 each year. Other exemptions and deferments, such as present-use value, must be filed by January 31.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Bladen County house with unpaid property taxes?
faqs.a: Yes. The closing attorney pays the delinquent taxes to the county tax collector from the sale proceeds, and the deed carries a statement saying so. The sale must close before the court confirms any tax foreclosure sale.
